narrative_purpose: Makes Ronal's judgement visible: a cylindrical tail and a flattened blade are different kinds of tool, and the difference decides how much thrust each stroke can produce.
subject: Two Na'vi tails shown side by side in the same stretch of clear open seawater, each attached to the lower back of a partially visible swimming body cropped at the waist. On the left, a slender cylindrical tail tapering to a small tuft of hair at its tip, angled mid-push with a churn of disturbed bubbles and broken swirls behind it. On the right, a broad flattened blade with no hair, dorsoventrally expanded and laterally compressed, angled mid-stroke with a smooth continuous sheet of clean flow bending around it and a tidy line of evenly spaced spiral eddies trailing behind.
scene: One continuous body of clear mid-depth seawater, both tails at the same depth and the same distance from the viewer, particles drifting in the light.
camera: Straight-on side view at tail height, both subjects at equal visual weight and identical scale.
light: Even cool blue-green light from above, cyan highlights on the wet skin of both tails, deep indigo in the water behind.
palette: Ocean teal and cyan for the clean flow on the right, muted grey-teal for the broken churn on the left, void indigo background.
style: Painterly naturalist comparison plate, organic and observed, not an infographic.
detail_level: Crisp on both tail surfaces and on the difference between churned bubbles and smooth flow; the water beyond kept simple.
composition: Left-to-right split with the two tails mirrored across the centre, open low-detail dark water in a band across the top of each half for overlay labels.
consistency_notes: Same water, same light, same scale on both halves. The left tail is unmistakably a round rope with a hair tuft; the right is unmistakably a flat hairless blade. Both are blue Na'vi skin, the left deeper cobalt and the right turquoise.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no panel borders or dividing lines, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
